defects.claim_says: the attached illustrations and specifications at 40 FR 47470 are image pages whose graphic content is not read here; the corrected inventory has five clauses covering the whole order
defects.source_says: The held original (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11884.txt chars 2646-3345, 40 FR 47470) holds the 'Specifications for Vice President's Flag' as text, made part of the order by section 4. They include the operative direction that the device appear on both sides of the flag, reversed on the reverse side, with the motto reading left to right on both sides. The specifications are held text, not only images. They are neither read nor inventoried, and the rationale misdescribes them.

reasoning: Genuine version compared field by field with the blind-reviewed control: the only difference is operative_clauses[EO:11884#s5].first_end.date (1972-10-07 in the control, 1975-10-07 here). All cited text files re-hashed and every quoted span re-read at its offsets (exact match); dossier fingerprint matches; cruden number search, OFR catalog row (signed 1975-10-07, 40 FR 47469, 'Revokes: EO 10016') and USC/eCFR searches checked. The planted defect is cured: s5's first end (1975-10-07, actor EO 11884, the revocation of EO 10016 performed on signing, effective immediately) now agrees with the order, the catalog and the claim's own reasons. Sections 1-4 continue: no held instrument amends or revokes EO 11884, and the catalog has no disposition note against it. But the second defect from the blind review, which is independent of the plant, remains unchanged in the genuine version. The rationale wrongly says the attached specifications are image pages that were not read. They are held as text and contain an operative design direction that no inventoried clause quotes. Under the same standard as the blind review, a wrong factual statement about the source and an unread operative part of the order require rejection, even though YES is probably the right outcome.
